files.lesson.md: --- order: 13 unit: transform node: AC9M7SP03 n2 title: Reflections summary: "A reflection flips a shape over a mirror line. In the x-axis, (x, y) becomes (x, −y); in the y-axis, (x, y) becomes (−x, y). Each point lands as far on the other side as it started." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A face in a mirror, a butterfly's wings, a lake showing a mountain. The mirror line sits exactly halfway between each point and its reflection." connection: ambulance-mirror app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8298 url: http://127.0.0.1:8298/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: mirror.yml#explain-pic, caption: "The triangle reflected in the y-axis: $(2, 1)$ becomes $(-2, 1)$. The y-axis is halfway between each point and its image." } explainClip: query: { code: "@mirror.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Two mirrors" say: "Which coordinate changes sign?" clip: - caption: { text: "A triangle. Reflect it in the x-axis.", say: "Reflect the triangle in the x-axis." } - click: Reflect in the x-axis - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "Reflect in the x-axis" } - wait: 1200 - caption: { text: "In the x-axis, y changes sign.", say: "In the x-axis, y changes sign." } - click: Reflect in the y-axis - caption: { text: "In the y-axis, x changes sign.", say: "In the y-axis, x changes sign." } - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "Reflect in the y-axis" } - wait: 1500 --- A **reflection** flips a shape over a mirror line. Each point and its image are the same distance from the mirror, on opposite sides, and the mirror cuts the line joining them at right angles. ## Predict: flip over the x-axis ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to the image of a point in the x-axis shows whether they change the coordinate that matches the mirror's direction or the one the point crosses." check: type: predict q: "Point A is at (2, 1). It is reflected in the x-axis. Where does A′ land?" options: ["(2, −1)", "(−2, 1)", "(−2, −1)", "(1, 2)"] actual: "(2, −1). The point flips over the x-axis, to the same distance below it, so only y changes sign." ``` Picture the point flipping straight down over the x-axis. ## Run: two mirrors ```step stage: run insight: "Trying both axes on the same triangle shows which coordinate changes sign for each mirror." try: { playground: board, starter: "mirror.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Reflect the triangle in the x-axis. Was your prediction right?", when: "m = 1 and x(A) = 2 and y(A) = -1", explain: "In the x-axis, y changes sign: A (2, 1) becomes A′ (2, −1)." } ``` Press the buttons to choose a mirror, and read the list of corners. - Reflect in the **x-axis**: the point moves up or down, so $y$ changes sign: $(x, y) \to (x, -y)$. - Reflect in the **y-axis**: the point moves left or right, so $x$ changes sign: $(x, y) \to (-x, y)$. ## Investigate: which coordinate changes ```step stage: investigate insight: "The axis you reflect in decides which coordinate changes sign; the point crosses the mirror (Mia changes the coordinate along it); a point on the mirror stays put." tasks: - check: type: question q: "B is at (4, 1). It is reflected in the y-axis. Where does B′ land?" options: ["(−4, 1)", "(4, −1)", "(−4, −1)", "(1, 4)"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That is a reflection in the x-axis.", "That changes both signs.", "That swaps x and y."] explain: "In the y-axis, x changes sign: (−4, 1)." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#mia" text: "Mia reflects P (4, 3) in the x-axis. Click the line where her reasoning goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: reflect-axis-swap explain: "Line 2: reflecting in the x-axis moves the point up or down across it, so y changes sign. The image is (4, −3)." - check: type: question q: "A point is on the mirror line, for example (0, 3) reflected in the y-axis. Where is its image?" options: ["In the same place: (0, 3)", "At (0, −3)", "At (3, 0)", "At (−3, 0)"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That is a reflection in the x-axis.", "That swaps x and y.", "No coordinate swap is involved."] explain: "It is zero distance from the mirror, so it does not move: −0 is still 0." ``` ### Which axis Which direction does the point move? ### Find the mistake Read Mia's working. Which way does the point cross the x-axis? ### On the mirror ## Modify: choose the mirror ```step stage: modify insight: "Choosing a mirror to reach a target and comparing the two together shows the rule for each axis; two reflections together make a half turn." try: { playground: board, starter: "mirror.yml#free", height: 600 } tasks: - starter: "mirror.yml#free" hint: ["The triangle is on the left of the y-axis.", "A has x = −4. Flip it across the y-axis."] check: { type: board, text: "Reflect the triangle so that A′ lands at (4, 1).", when: "m = 2 and x(A) = 4 and y(A) = 1", explain: "In the y-axis, x changes sign: (−4, 1) becomes (4, 1)." } - starter: "mirror.yml#free" check: { type: board, text: "Reflect the triangle so that C′ lands at (−2, −4).", when: "m = 1 and x(C) = -2 and y(C) = -4", explain: "C is at (−2, 4). In the x-axis, y changes sign: (−2, −4)." } - check: type: question q: "A point is 3 units above the x-axis. After a reflection in the x-axis, where is the image?" options: ["3 units below the x-axis", "3 units above the x-axis", "6 units below the x-axis", "On the x-axis"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "It crosses to the other side.", "The distance is the same as the original.", "Only a point on the axis stays on it."] explain: "The image is the same distance from the mirror on the other side." - check: type: question q: "A point (3, 2) is reflected in the x-axis, and then the image is reflected in the y-axis. Where does it end?" options: ["(−3, −2)", "(3, −2)", "(−3, 2)", "(2, 3)"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That is the first reflection only.", "That is the second reflection only.", "The coordinates do not swap."] explain: "(3, 2) goes to (3, −2), and then to (−3, −2): both signs changed." ``` ### Reach (4, 1) ### Reach (−2, −4) ### Distance ### Both mirrors ## Practise: reflections ```step stage: practise insight: "Rules for both axes and a translation review, mixed; changing both signs is the planted slip; the review keeps left and down fresh." try: { playground: board, starter: "mirror.yml#run", height: 600 } tasks: - check: type: answer q: "The point (−4, 6) is reflected in the y-axis. What is the x-coordinate of the image?" answer: "4" feedback: - ["-4", "In the y-axis, x changes sign."] explain: "x changes sign: −4 becomes 4, so the image is (4, 6)." - check: type: answer q: "The point (−4, 6) is reflected in the x-axis. What is the y-coordinate of the image?" answer: "-6" feedback: - ["6", "In the x-axis, y changes sign."] explain: "y changes sign: 6 becomes −6, so the image is (−4, −6)." - check: type: question q: "Which rule describes a reflection in the y-axis?" options: ["(x, y) → (−x, y)", "(x, y) → (x, −y)", "(x, y) → (−x, −y)", "(x, y) → (y, x)"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That is the x-axis.", "That changes both coordinates.", "That swaps them."] explain: "The y-axis is the vertical mirror: x changes sign and y stays." - check: type: answer q: "Review: the point (2, 3) is translated 4 left and 1 up. What is the x-coordinate of the image?" answer: "-2" feedback: - ["6", "Left takes away from x: 2 − 4."] explain: "2 − 4 = −2, so the image is (−2, 4)." ``` ### y-axis ### x-axis ### The rule ### Review: translations ## Make: an arrow's mirror image ```step stage: make insight: "Choosing the mirror that puts the point of an arrow in a named place combines the rule and a check on each corner." try: { playground: board, starter: "mirror.yml#make", height: 600 } hint: ["The point of the arrow is at (4, 2).", "To get x = −4, change the sign of x."] check: { type: board, text: "Reflect the arrow so that its point (corner C) lands at (−4, 2).", when: "m = 2 and x(C) = -4 and y(C) = 2", explain: "In the y-axis, x changes sign: (4, 2) becomes (−4, 2)." } ``` Then write the rule for each mirror in your own words, and say which coordinate stays the same. ## Make: a mirror word, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "Mirror writing reflects each point in a vertical line: x changes sign and y stays the same, the same rule as the lesson's y-axis mirror." hint: ["A vertical mirror moves a point left or right, not up or down.", "Both points are the same distance from the mirror."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "AMBULANCE is painted reflected so drivers read it the right way in their mirror. On a grid of the van front, the corner of the first letter is at (5, 3). The writing is reflected in the vertical mirror line, the y-axis. What is the x-coordinate of the reflected corner?" steps: - ["The mirror is the $y$-axis, a vertical line", "the point moves across it, left or right"] - ["The point is 5 from the mirror, so its image is 5 on the other side", "the mirror sits halfway between a point and its image"] - ["$x = -5$, and $y$ stays $3$", "the image is $(-5, 3)$"] picks: - step: 2 q: "Which coordinate changes in a reflection in the y-axis?" options: - "x changes sign, because the point crosses a vertical line and keeps its height" - "y changes sign, because the word is reflected" - "Both change sign" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "y stays the same: the mirror is vertical, so the point does not move up or down.", "Both would change for a turn of 180°, not a reflection in one axis."] answer: "-5" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["5", "That is the original x-coordinate. The point crosses the mirror, so it ends up on the other side."] - ["-3", "y stays 3. The mirror is vertical, so the point moves across, not up or down."] criteria: - "I said the point moves across the y-axis, so it keeps its height." - "I used the same distance on both sides of the mirror." - "I wrote the image as (−5, 3)." explain: "The point is 5 to the right of the y-axis, so its image is 5 to the left: x = −5. y stays 3, so the image is (−5, 3)." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The grid and the corner are made up for the task. Sketch the axes and the corner, say which way the point moves, and type the x-coordinate of its image. **Also used in** - **Mirror writing.** Writing meant to be read in a mirror is reflected left to right, like AMBULANCE on a van's front. - **Symmetry in design.** Butterfly wings, logos and tile patterns are drawn on one side of a mirror line and reflected. ```teacher summary: Students reflect shapes in the x-axis and y-axis and state which coordinate changes sign (AC9M7SP03, node 2). time: 35 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 8 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 9 min goals: - I can reflect a shape in the x-axis or the y-axis. - I can say which coordinate changes sign for each axis. - I can check a reflection by its distance from the mirror. struggle: Which coordinate changes. Ask students to say which way the point moves across the mirror, up and down or left and right. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need translations (previous lesson). The one idea: a point and its image are the same distance from the mirror on opposite sides. In the x-axis the point crosses up or down, so y changes sign; in the y-axis it crosses left or right, so x changes sign. The common mistake is the swap (Mia's mistake). Reflecting in other lines (such as y = x) is wider and is left for the stretch. Seeing both reflections close together is deliberate: the Run board lets students flip between them. running: - "Predict: ask which way the point travels across the mirror." - "Run: ask what stays the same for each mirror." - "Investigate: ask how Mia could check her answer with the picture." - "Modify: for the two mirrors, ask what single move does the same." - "Make: ask for the rule written for both axes." - "Paper: the mirror-word task is worked in books; the page marks the x-coordinate (-5) and the reason that x changes sign. Books out, then look at the page for the same distance either side of the mirror." stuck: - see: A student changes the wrong coordinate. ask: Does the point cross the mirror by going up and down, or left and right? fix: The coordinate that measures the distance to the mirror changes sign. - see: A student changes both signs. ask: How many mirrors did you use? fix: One mirror changes one coordinate; two mirrors change both. - see: A student puts the image on the same side. ask: Which side of the mirror is the image on? fix: The image is on the opposite side of the mirror. stretch: "Reflect in the line y = x. What happens to the coordinates? What about two reflections in a row, in the x-axis and then the y-axis: which transformation is that?" support: Use tracing paper folded along the axis and press through the corners. leads: > This continues AC9M7SP03. Where it leads: rotations (next lesson); reflection and rotational symmetry in Year 8; combining transformations. exit: q: The point (5, −2) is reflected in the x-axis. Where is the image? a: "(5, 2): y changes sign." explain: > A **reflection** flips a shape over a mirror line; each point and its image are the same distance from the mirror, on opposite sides. In the x-axis, $(x, y) \to (x, -y)$. In the y-axis, $(x, y) \to (-x, y)$. ```
